title: Finding the real online store
prompt: You want to buy a new electric kettle from Maple Market. Which web address is the real store?

reasons.opt-real: This is the real store domain with no extra words or weird endings.
reasons.opt-fake: Fake shopping sites add words like "clearance" or "90off" to lure you in and steal card details.

explanation: Scammers create look-alike shopping sites that advertise 80% to 90% discounts on popular goods. The items never arrive, and the criminals steal your credit card information. Always verify the address.
takeaways: Unbelievable discounts are almost always fake.
Check the domain carefully before buying.

title: Buyer sending an extra check for your furniture

segments.text: Hello, I am glad to purchase your dining table set for the listed $400.
My office accountant accidentally made out the cashier's check for $1,200 instead of $400.

flag.reason: Overpayment checks are a guaranteed scam. Legitimate buyers do not accidentally send hundreds of extra dollars.

segments.text: Please deposit the $1,200 check, keep $100 for your trouble, and wire the remaining $700 back to my movers today.

flag.reason: The scammer wants you to send your own real cash before the fake check bounces days or weeks later.

segments.text: The moving truck will arrive once you confirm the wire transfer.

explanation: Banks are required by law to make check funds available within a few days, but verifying a forged cashier's check can take weeks. When it bounces, you are legally responsible for all funds you wired away.
takeaways: Never accept a check for more than the selling price.
Never wire back part of a check payment.

title: Assessing a 90% off social media shopping ad
prompt: A sponsored social media ad shows a $400 outdoor winter jacket on sale for $39 with free shipping. Which action is safe?

options.label: Ignore the ad and search for the jacket directly on the manufacturer's official website
Click the link and purchase immediately using your debit card before the 10-minute timer expires

reasons.a: Correct: 90% discounts on premium goods advertised on social media almost always lead to fraudulent stores that steal debit card numbers.
reasons.b: Risky: The countdown clock is manufactured panic designed to make you type payment details before you notice the site is counterfeit.

explanation: Scammers buy social media ads promoting unbelievable discounts on brand-name products. Victims either receive counterfeit goods or nothing at all while having their payment cards compromised.
takeaways: Unbelievable social media discounts usually lead to counterfeit storefronts.
Look up products directly on authorized retailer websites.
